Package neqsim.process.fielddevelopment.wellplanning

Class DriftFluxWellboreHydraulics

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.fielddevelopment.wellplanning.DriftFluxWellboreHydraulics
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class DriftFluxWellboreHydraulics extends Object implements Serializable
Mechanistic drift-flux hydraulics for vertical and deviated production tubing with flow-regime, liquid-loading and erosional-velocity output.

The pressure traverse is integrated segment by segment with NeqSim flashes at the local pressure and temperature. The gradient is gravity plus wall friction. Liquid holdup comes from the drift-flux relation alpha = v_sg / (C0 v_m + v_d) with Hasan and Kabir style closures:

  • bubble flow (alpha up to 0.25): C0 = 1.2, v_d = 1.53 (g sigma d_rho / rho_L^2)^0.25 sqrt(sin theta)
  • slug flow (alpha below 0.52): C0 = 1.2, Taylor bubble v_d = (0.35 sin theta + 0.54 cos theta) sqrt(g D d_rho / rho_L)
  • churn flow: C0 = 1.15 with the Taylor bubble drift velocity
  • annular flow (v_sg at or above the Turner/Wallis film-reversal velocity 3.1 (sigma g d_rho / rho_G^2)^0.25 and beyond the slug limit): Wallis void fraction alpha = (1 + X^0.8)^-0.378 with the Lockhart-Martinelli parameter X

Liquid loading onset is flagged when v_sg falls below the Turner critical velocity. The erosional velocity is the API RP 14E value v_e = C / sqrt(rho_ns) with C = 100 (lb/ft3)^0.5 ft/s by default.

Limitations: screening-level; acceleration pressure drop, emulsion viscosity, liquid entrainment fractions and stratified flow in near-horizontal sections are not modelled (a warning is issued below 10 degrees from horizontal). Validation is limited to analytic limits (single-phase Darcy-Weisbach, static column) and comparison with Beggs and Brill; it is not calibrated to field data.
